title: sequence and string dynamic programming
concepts: Sequence DP often defines a state over a prefix, ending position, or pair of positions, with transitions that match, skip, extend, or restart a candidate subsequence.
A subsequence preserves relative order but may skip elements; a substring is contiguous, so their recurrences and boundary rules differ.
Longest common subsequence uses two prefix indices and considers matching characters or skipping one side; reconstruction follows stored or recomputed choices.
Longest increasing subsequence has an O(n²) endpoint DP and an O(n log n) tails optimization that stores minimum tail values rather than the full subsequence history.
String edit distance uses prefix pairs and models insert, delete, and replace operations; initialization handles converting a prefix to or from an empty string.
Palindromic substring problems depend on contiguous ranges and interval expansion, while palindromic subsequence problems allow skipped characters and use interval states.
Space compression for two-string DP can retain adjacent rows, but direction and reconstruction requirements may prevent discarding earlier state.
Common errors include off-by-one prefix indexing, confusing substring with subsequence, and omitting empty-prefix base cases.

practiceProblems.name: Longest Common Subsequence
practiceProblems.statement: Return the length of the longest common subsequence of two strings; a subsequence preserves order and may omit characters.
constraints: Both strings contain lowercase English letters

practiceProblems.name: Longest Increasing Subsequence
practiceProblems.statement: Return the length of the longest strictly increasing subsequence in an integer array.
constraints: The problem includes an O(n log n) follow-up

practiceProblems.name: Maximum Length of Repeated Subarray
practiceProblems.statement: Return the maximum length of a contiguous subarray appearing in both integer arrays.

practiceProblems.name: Palindromic Substrings
practiceProblems.statement: Count positional occurrences of palindromic substrings; equal text at different positions counts multiple times.
constraints: s consists of lowercase English letters

practiceProblems.name: Longest Palindromic Subsequence
patterns: match endpoints or discard one endpoint
practiceProblems.statement: Return the length of the longest palindromic subsequence of a string.
constraints: s consists of lowercase English letters

practiceProblems.name: Word Break
practiceProblems.statement: Return whether s can be segmented into one or more dictionary words; dictionary words may be reused.
constraints: s and dictionary words contain lowercase English letters

practiceProblems.name: Minimum ASCII Delete Sum for Two Strings
practiceProblems.statement: Return the minimum sum of deleted character ASCII values needed to make two strings equal using deletions only.
constraints: Both strings contain lowercase English letters
The result fits a signed 32-bit integer

practiceProblems.name: Regular Expression Matching
practiceProblems.statement: Return whether the pattern matches the entire string; dot matches any one character and star matches zero or more repetitions of the preceding valid element.
constraints: p contains lowercase English letters, dot, and star
Every star has a preceding valid element
